chunks: From him, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb al-Naysaburi, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, regarding what is known from Nadir the servant,
He said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) mentioned celery, so he said: 'You all desire it, and there is no animal except that it rubs itself with it.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida say about the scent and popularity of celery?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) highlights the universal appeal of celery (*kafs*) by noting that while humans crave it, all other animals also rub themselves against it, indicating its potent scent and widespread desirability across species. This observation reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of deriving practical wisdom from everyday natural phenomena, illustrating how divine creation endows certain substances with unique qualities that bridge human and animal nature.
